diagnoses.summary: PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with a strong signal on the reflux subsystem, dominated by a failed reflux pump trip. Likely cause is the reflux pump trip fault propagating through the reflux circuit.

The PCA abnormal state is most consistent with a failure in the H2 PCV (cstr_vent_valve) causing reactor pressure to rise and alarms on reactor pressure high/high-high. The top contributing variables point to the CSTR pressure and H2 vent, with PCV-related faults aligning with the observed pattern.

The PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with significant reactor pressure rise and a strong contribution from the H2 vent path. The most likely fault is a restriction on the H2 PCV outlet causing pressure to increase and trigger high-pressure alarms.

Both Hotelling T² and SPE are violated with a coherent plant upset centered on reactor pressure, driven by the H2 PCV path. The strongest evidence points to a fault in the H2 PCV valve leading to restricted venting.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset dominated by H2 vent (PCV) dynamics and reactor pressure rise, with the strongest evidence pointing to the H2 PCV (PCV) being stuck/limited in opening, causing pressure buildup and compensatory responses downstream.

PCA flags a large, coherent disturbance with strong involvement of the H2 vent (PCV) and reactor pressure rise. The most likely fault is a problem with the H2 PCV (vent valve) causing pressure to climb and triggering high-pressure alarms.
PCA indicates a large, coherent upset centered on reactor pressure/venting with hydrogen vent contributing most; likely H2 PCV fault causing inadequate venting and pressure rise.

PCA detects a large, coherent plant upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations. Top contributor is the reflux control path, suggesting a reflux flow actuator issue propagating through the distillation stage.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with strong correlation to condenser/column related disturbances; high T² and high SPE point to a new/altered correlation pattern consistent with condenser cooling issue propagating through the column.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with strong SPE indicating a process/wet-utility issue propagating through the distillation section; several rule-based hypotheses point to condenser cooling loss and related upstream valve/loop saturation.

PCA signals a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations. Most consistent with condenser cooling effectiveness loss causing distillation instability and elevated temperatures, with a secondary tendency toward RB_LIC saturation (controller out of range) and possible H2 PCV related issue.

PCA detects a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violated. Strong evidence points to a condenser cooling impairment propagating through the column, with secondary effects triggering the RBLIC control saturation and a distillate/temperature interaction.

Congruent large upset with strong distillate acetone deviation and condenser-related signals; condenser cooling efficiency loss is most likely responsible for the abnormal PCA, with a contributing saturation in the RB_LIC loop.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong SPE, dominated by distillate acetone and column temperatures; DIST_X_L alarm active and RB_LIC loop saturated. Most consistent with a condenser cooling loss causing reduced condenser duty and shifted distillation feedback.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with strong disturbance to the distillation column, dominated by distillate composition and column/tray conditions, with an active DIST_X_L alarm and a saturated RB_LIC loop. The most likely fault is loss of condenser cooling effectiveness causing abnormal distillate composition and column dynamics; RB_LIC saturation supports a downstream condenser-related upset.

PCA detects a large, coherent plant upset with strong distillate composition deviation in the distillate stream, dominated by condenser-related symptoms and a saturated reflux/drum control loop. The most likely cause is condenser cooling effectiveness loss driving abnormal distillate composition and column behavior.

PCA indicates a coherent upset with large T2 and large SPE violations; most consistent with a condenser cooling effectiveness issue propagating through the column, supported by active DIST_X_L alarm and SPE/contributions. RB_LIC out of range is a plausible secondary fault due to loop saturation while plant attempts to compensate.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with concurrent SPE violation and a DIST_X_L alarm. The most consistent fault is condenser cooling effectiveness loss, with an additional possible RB_LIC out-of-range (loop saturation) contributing to the upset.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations and an active DIST_X_L alarm. Evidence points to a loss of condenser cooling effectiveness driving abnormal distillate composition and column dynamics. RB_LIC saturation is also present, suggesting upstream control struggle possibly linked to the condenser fault.

PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with a strong disturbance in the distillate acetone signal and an active DIST_X_L alarm. Evidence points to degradation in condenser cooling efficiency driving the column upset and the distillate composition reading anomaly.
PCA anomaly with large coherent upset; evidence points to condenser cooling issue as the primary fault, with secondary plant upsets possible (reboiler/flows).

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations and a plant-wide disturbance centred on the distillation train. The fixed-rule evidence points to a condenser cooling issue causing abnormal distillate composition and temperature signals.

PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with both T² and SPE violations. The strongest rule-based hint points to condenser cooling limitations driving the abnormal state, consistent with high acetone distillate deviations and column pressure effects.
PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with both T2 and SPE violations; most likely a condenser cooling fault causing distillate quality alarm and upstream controller saturation.
